title: Autoswitch protection policy for surge and error patterns
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We currently rely on simple threshold gates for fallbacks (percent 429s or absolute error counts) which either trigger too late or oscillate during bursty traffic. That leads to increased tail latency for affected customers and noisy operator interventions. We need a protective "autoswitch" policy that blends multiple signals, applies tenant-aware weighting, and enforces hysteresis and cooldown so fallbacks are automatic, predictable, and reversible without thrashing.

Goal: Define and implement an autoswitch protection policy that: 1) detects emergent overload/error patterns quickly (429 spikes, timeouts, sudden p95/p99 regressions, and downstream model variants returning errors), 2) safely transitions traffic to a fallback model variant (lower-cost/quantized variant or replica in another region/tier) when confidence is high, 3) applies decay/hysteresis and exponential cooldown so routing flips don’t cause oscillation, 4) exposes clear telemetry and debug traces for triage, and 5) supports per-tenant overrides and canary rollouts.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement autoscaling or capacity provisioning policies; it focuses on routing decision logic and policy enforcement. It also does not modify model weights/quantization itself; fallbacks use pre-provisioned variants.

High-level approach:
- Multi-signal scoring: compute a rolling "trip score" combining weighted signals: 429 rate, timeout rate, 5xx error rate, sudden increase in generation token latency (p95/p99 delta), and model-specific error signals (decode failures, OOMs). Each signal is normalized by baseline and smoothed with EWMA.
- Tenant weighting: compute score per tenant by normalizing by tenant baseline traffic and by configured tenant-priority multiplier (enterprise tenants can have higher trip thresholds).
- Bayesian confidence window: require sustained elevated score over two window sizes (short 30s window + medium 5m window) and a posterior confidence > 0.9 before triggering autoswitch. This reduces sensitivity to microbursts.
- Fallback selection: rank available fallback variants by compatibility and allowed degradation profile (regionally compatible first, then lower-accuracy quantized variants, then cross-region). Each candidate has an estimated latency/cost/quality delta. We prefer candidates that maintain SLOs with minimal quality loss.
acceptance_criteria: Trip score computed and emitted for each request path and tenant (metric: routing.trip_score)
Auto-switch triggers when short+medium windows exceed configured thresholds and posterior confidence >= 0.9
Fallback chosen using deterministic ranking; candidate and reason emitted to logs/trace
Hysteresis enforced: minimum protection hold time (configurable) and exponential backoff cooldown with jitter
No flip-flop observed in load tests that simulate oscillating 429 patterns for 30 minutes
Dashboard panel added showing trip score, signal components, and active fallbacks by tenant
implementation_notes: Create new routing decision module (AutoswitchController) in routing-service with a pluggable scoring pipeline
Implement EWMA smoothing and Bayesian window evaluation in C++ for low-latency scoring; expose config via feature flags
Fallback ranking table stored in metadata DB (readonly for decision path); include model variant metadata (latency_est, quality_est, region, tier)
Add tracing annotations for decision rationale: scores, windows, selected fallback, cooldown deadlines
Unit + integration tests: simulate multi-tenant traffic with synthetic 429/timeout patterns and validate triggers and cooldown behavior
test_plan: Local harness: inject signals (429, timeouts, p99 spikes) and assert trip_score progression and trigger timing
Staging: run a canary with 5% of traffic routed through AutoswitchController for 48 hours; monitor false positive rate and customer-visible latency
Chaos test: induce region flaps and ensure cross-region fallbacks trigger only after confidence threshold
Load test: replay production-like traces for 2h with oscillations; measure flip-rate < 0.1 per minute per route
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (0%-5%): Enable AutoswitchController in passive mode (emit decisions but do not enforce) for 72h to collect signal distributions
Phase 2 (5%-25%): Enforce autoswitch for non-enterprise tenants with conservative thresholds and 10s hold time
Phase 3 (25%-100%): Gradually widen to all tenants with tenant-specific thresholds and enable enterprise overrides
Rollback: instant disable feature flag and explicit revert to last stable routing policy; record event and notify on-call

risks: False positives during sudden traffic shifts could route traffic to lower-quality variants—mitigated by conservative confidence thresholds and canary rollouts
Performance overhead if scoring is implemented in interpreted layers—mitigated by native EWMA implementation and microbenchmarks
Operational complexity: new metrics and cooldown windows require SRE training and runbook updates
